issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters and returning an int, but the solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This parameter mismatch also causes other methods in the solution (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to call getTotalNumberOfStudents(true), relying on the boolean parameter. Students following the UML and task text (which expect a no-argument method) will be confused or unable to match the provided solution/signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across the artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters (and adjust getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor to use the no-arg version), or (B) update the UML/problem statement to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) so the parameter is documented. Ensure the template, problem text/UML, and solution all use the same signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns an int. The solution implementation provides getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) (a different signature). This mismatch between the expected method name/signature and the solution creates a cognitive mapping barrier: students looking for or asked to implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no args) will find a differently named/typed method in the solution, and may be confused whether a boolean parameter is required or optional.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/UML by providing the no-argument method signature public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total (inscribed + guest). If conditional behavior is desired, either overload the method (add public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) while keeping the no-arg version, or update the problem statement/UML to explicitly require a boolean parameter. Prefer keeping the no-arg method to match the assignment text and UML.
